subject: Nanotechnology
title: Pseudocapacitance
description: A quick, practical guide to Pseudocapacitance.

hook.text: Batteries are slow but store a lot — capacitors are fast but store little. Pseudocapacitors do both.

buildup.text: Surface redox reactions at nanostructured oxide electrodes store charge — faradaic but capacitor-fast.

discovery.text: RuO₂ nanoparticles show near-ideal pseudocapacitance — 900 F/g with no diffusion limitation at nanoscale.

twist.text: Ruthenium is rare and expensive — MnO₂ and Fe₃O₄ nano alternatives trade some performance for affordability.

climax.text: Hybrid devices pair a pseudocapacitive electrode with a battery electrode — capturing both speed and energy.

punchline.text: Surface chemistry at nanoscale bridges the gap between batteries and capacitors.

quiz.question: What is pseudocapacitance?
options: Charge storage that only works at cryogenic temperatures
Fast surface redox reactions at nanostructured electrodes that store charge like a battery at capacitor speed
Capacitance created by stacking multiple capacitors in series
